clue.text: New northern theatre put in jeopardy

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly opened theatre in the north faces a threat to its future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges N (northern) together with THEATRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace something or put it at risk is to place it in jeopardy.

clue.text: Emphasizes decapitation — removing these, presumably

indicators.note: decapitation cuts off the head, so the opening letter of the word for emphasizes goes

parts.note: to emphasize is to stress, giving stresses

explanation.surface: Beheading someone would presumably take their long hair off with the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitation' removes the first S of STRESSES; the whole clue also describes the answer, since beheading would carry off a person's locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks of long hair would go with the head in a beheading.

clue.text: Remember to pass the hat round again

parts.note: RE- is the prefix meaning again
passing the hat round is taking a collection of money

explanation.surface: A reminder to take up a second collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; split the answer as RE-COLLECT to see the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something to mind is to remember it.

clue.text: Incite to sin? At first it's an effort

indicators.note: first places the little word at the front of the charade, ahead of the rest

parts.note: to tempt is to entice someone into wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Encouraging wickedness is hard work at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'Incite to sin' look like a question, but it is just a word for entice; 'first' only orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A try or endeavour is an effort.

clue.text: Understanding several points about wine

indicators.note: about means the points go round the word for wine, enclosing it

parts.note: E, N and E are compass points, together east-north-east
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A discussion of wine yields agreement on several points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'several points' means compass points, not a list of matters agreed; tent is an old name for a Spanish red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations, a mutual understanding.

clue.text: Turn around outside your entrance

indicators.note: outside means the word for entrance sits round the abbreviation

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn back at the gate to someone's property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your entrance' reads as someone's front door, but 'your' is only the abbreviation, held inside the gate by 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin or revolve is to turn around.

clue.text: A runner like John Halifax

definitions.meaning: a smuggler, one who runs contraband; old slang called smugglers gentlemen
the hero of Dinah Craik's novel John Halifax

explanation.walkthrough: The 'runner' is not an athlete but a smuggler, as in gun-runner; Kipling's poem calls smugglers 'the Gentlemen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smugglers were euphemistically called gentlemen, and Craik's title names her hero as a man of good breeding.

clue.text: Followers may be inert and extremely unreliable

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else when shuffled
extremely takes the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Hangers-on may turn out lazy and untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges INERT to RETIN; 'extremely' takes U and E from unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a body of attendants who follow an important person.

clue.text: Leader of troops managed to rest in this camp

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means managed
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: The commanding officer arranged for the soldiers to rest at this camp.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: a transit camp is a temporary camp for people on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: A transit camp houses troops or refugees briefly while they are passing through.

clue.text: Old mention in dispatches produces stirring emotion

parts.note: EX is the prefix for former or old
a soldier mentioned in dispatches receives a citation

explanation.surface: Being commended in military dispatches is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Excitation is the act of arousing feeling, a stirring up.

clue.text: He's contemptible compared with a Democrat

parts.note: to means compared with, as in nothing to him

explanation.surface: A partisan sneer at a politician in comparison with a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: TO in the sense of 'in comparison with' (ten to one) is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A toad is a loathsome person, a common insult.

clue.text: Wise man with one son has estates in the Pacific

parts.note: King Solomon was proverbially wise
I is the Roman numeral one
lands are estates

explanation.surface: A wise father with an only son owns property in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'has' are link words; the definition only places the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This island nation lies in the south-west Pacific, east of Papua New Guinea.

clue.text: Ghost of police officer in this, say?

definitions.text: Ghost of police officer in this, say?

parts.words: Ghost of police officer in this, say?
parts.note: a ghost word which, put after 'in', sounds like a senior police rank, so the officer is 'in' this ghost

explanation.walkthrough: Say the police rank inspector slowly: it sounds like 'in' plus the ghost word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectral apparition is a ghost or phantom.

clue.text: Crisis for supporter of outspoken old antimonarchist

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece holds up the first, so the crisis word acts as support beneath the outspoken word

parts.note: round means blunt or outspoken, as in a round rebuke
a head is a crisis point, as in come to a head

explanation.surface: A political crisis for a supporter of an outspoken republican of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for supporter of' works because in a down answer the second piece sits beneath the first, holding it up; 'outspoken' means blunt here, not a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundheads were the Parliamentarians who fought King Charles I in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Pardon for girl accepting shelter

indicators.note: accepting means the girl's name takes the other word inside it

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
a nest is a shelter

explanation.surface: A girl who took someone in is let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' is the container signal: the girl takes the shelter in, as a host takes in a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon, often for many offenders at once.

clue.text: One proceeding with difficulty when preparing eggs

definitions.meaning: a person clambering or struggling along
someone beating eggs in a pan while they cook

explanation.walkthrough: 'One' serves both halves: a person who clambers, and a person who scrambles eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble is both to climb awkwardly and to cook beaten eggs while stirring.

clue.text: Unusually quaint Oriental relic

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: E for East is the crossword abbreviation for Oriental

explanation.surface: A curiously charming Eastern relic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges QUAINT to ANTIQU.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is an old object, a relic of the past.

clue.text: Grannie eager to get material

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
keen means eager

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic grandmother wants to buy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing.

clue.text: Paddy's claim to be anti- English? Fancy

parts.note: an Irishman saying in dialect 'I'm agin', meaning I am against

explanation.surface: An Irishman claims to be hostile to the English, or so you'd think.
explanation.walkthrough: AGIN is dialect for against; 'Paddy' is an old nickname for an Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to suppose or picture it in the mind.

clue.text: In margin insert note for temporary

indicators.note: insert means the musical note goes into the middle of the preceding words

parts.note: a rim is an edge or margin
TE is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An instruction to add a provisional note in the margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insert' is the container signal; 'note' is the sol-fa note, not a written jotting.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is one holding only for the time being.

clue.text: Very much in verbal form

parts.note: a tense is a form of a verb showing time

explanation.surface: A remark about something set down in verb form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbal form' means a form of a verb, not something spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means extreme or existing to a high degree.

clue.text: Defame university chancellors originally in commerce

indicators.note: in means the shorter pieces are placed inside the word for commerce

parts.note: trade is commerce

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the word chancellors

explanation.surface: University chancellors accused of slandering people in the business world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U and C inside TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to slander them, damaging their reputation.

clue.text: Wealthy Scotsman made an observation

parts.note: mon is a Scots way of saying man, so a Scotsman
eyed means watched or observed

explanation.surface: A rich Scot passed comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made an observation' looks like speech but means watched.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed people are rich, having plenty of cash.

clue.text: Old person's quarters given free land at Arnhem

parts.note: N and E are two quarters of the compass, north and east

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier's billet granted on liberated ground at the Dutch city of Arnhem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges the ten letters of 'land at Arnhem' after the two compass quarters; Arnhem is a Dutch city famous for a 1944 battle.
explanation.definitionFit: This extinct human species lived in Europe tens of thousands of years ago, an ancient person.

clue.text: Hat to some extent like Pierrot's

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hat a bit like the one worn by Pierrot the clown.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap with a flat top and a peak.

clue.text: What happens to everybody's friend in the end

parts.note: an event is something that happens
U is the British film rating meaning suitable for everybody
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A reflection on the fate of a universally popular friend.
explanation.walkthrough: U (universal) is the British certificate for films anyone may see.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means finally, after some time.

clue.text: Like the four central characters in 25 — truly

annotationWithheld.why: Like the four central characters in 25 — truly: the central four letters of 25 (DEFERRED) are FERR, not DEED, so the cross-reference gives no wordplay for the answer
annotationWithheld.clue: Like the four central characters in 25 — truly

clue.text: Submitted' to being put on ice

explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link; to defer to someone is to submit to them.
explanation.definitionFit: One who deferred to another gave way to them, and a plan deferred has been shelved for later.
